extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel in inter partes proceedings before the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules and best practices governing discovery in TTAB trademark proceedings, including requests for production, requests for admission, ESI production, timing, place/form of production, privilege logs, and the duty to cooperate and confer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of a Request for Production (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must (A) describe with reasonable particularity each item or category of items to be inspected; (B) specify a reasonable time, place, and manner for the inspection and for performing the related acts; and (C) may specify the form or forms in which electronically stored information is to be produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for production must include the elements specified in Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(1)(A)-(B). Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(1)(C) allows but does not require specifying preferred data format(s) for ESI; parties are expected to discuss production format during the mandatory discovery conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussing ESI production form during discovery conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are expected to discuss the format for production of electronically stored information during their mandatory discovery conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(1)(C) and TBMP encourage parties to negotiate ESI form. See TBMP §§ 401.01 and 408.01(a) for discovery conference guidance and examples (e.g., parties agreeing only to the form of ESI production).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to respond to a Request for Production
rubrics_metrics.description: The party to whom the request is directed must respond in writing within 30 days after being served (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(2)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must be served within 30 days unless otherwise stipulated or ordered. If service was by first-class mail, Express Mail, or overnight courier, the mailing/delivery date is date of service and five extra days are allowed; no extra time for agreed electronic service (fax/email). Failure to respond may forfeit the right to object on the merits (motion to compel may seek such a finding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of responses to each item (produce or object with reasons)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each item or category, the response must either state that inspection and related activities will be permitted as requested or state an objection to the request, including the reasons (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(2)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper response should state whether responsive documents exist and, if so, whether they will be produced or withheld on a claim of privilege. If accurate, a party may respond that documents do not exist or are not in its possession/custody/control. It is generally inappropriate to attack requests by motion instead of responding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial objections must specify the part and permit inspection of the rest
rubrics_metrics.description: An objection to part of a request must specify the part and permit inspection of the rest (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(2)(C)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If objection is made to only part of an item or category, the part must be specified so the remaining non‑objected material is available for inspection/production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to requests for production of ESI (form objections and disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The response may state an objection to a requested form for producing ESI. If the responding party objects to a requested form — or if no form was specified — the party must state the form or forms it intends to use (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(2)(D)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no form specified, produce ESI in form(s) it is ordinarily maintained or in a reasonably usable form. The responding party must state what form(s) it will use if it objects. Parties should attempt to resolve ESI form and related issues in the discovery conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing documents as kept in the ordinary course or organized/labeled to correspond
rubrics_metrics.description: A party must produce documents as they are kept in the usual course of business or must organize and label them to correspond to the categories in the request (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(2)(E)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents produced in ESI form not kept in the ordinary course must be organized and labeled to correspond to the categories in each request. The Board encourages exchanging copies of documents by forwarding them to requesting party (often more efficient).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of ESI production when unspecified: ordinarily maintained or reasonably usable
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request does not specify a form for producing ESI, a party must produce it in a form or forms in which it is ordinarily maintained or in a reasonably usable form or forms (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(2)(E)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary, a responding party must 'translate' information into a reasonably usable form. However, producing in a 'reasonably usable' form does not permit converting ESI to a form that makes it more difficult or burdensome for the requesting party to use the information efficiently. A party need not produce the same ESI in more than one form.

rubrics_metrics.name: A party need not produce same ESI in more than one form
rubrics_metrics.description: A party need not produce the same electronically stored information in more than one form (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(2)(E)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits the responding party's obligation to duplicate ESI production across formats, unless otherwise stipulated or ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and indexing of large productions
rubrics_metrics.description: Large or complex productions should be organized and indexed to correspond to discovery requests and categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for documents produced on DVD, the Board ordered a complete index cross-referencing the categories and discovery requests, with no category in the index to exceed 300 pages (Amazon Technologies, Inc. v. Wax). Providing indices facilitates use and review of large productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation to create documents that do not exist
rubrics_metrics.description: A party is not under an obligation to create or prepare documents that do not already exist in response to a discovery request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production cannot be required of a document no longer in existence nor of one yet to be prepared. A party may respond that requested documents are lost, destroyed, or otherwise non-existent if accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of production governed by 37 CFR § 2.120(d)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The production of documents and things will be made at the place where the documents and things are usually kept, or where the parties agree, or where and in the manner which the Board, upon motion, orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party is obliged to make documents available for inspection and copying where stored and as kept in the ordinary course of business or as organized/labeled to correspond to requests. Parties often agree to copy and forward documents at the requesting party's expense; the Board encourages this as efficient. On motion the Board may specify place/manner and form of production and may order photocopying and mailing (potentially as a sanction).

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI production should not be made in a form that hampers use
rubrics_metrics.description: Producing ESI in a 'reasonably usable' form does not allow converting ESI from the form in which it is maintained to a different form that makes it more difficult or burdensome for the requesting party to use efficiently in the litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding parties should not use form conversion to obstruct access; parties should discuss protocols for identifying/segregating responsive ESI and search methods during the discovery conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI production protocols to discuss
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects of ESI production other than form that should be discussed include a protocol for identifying and segregating potentially responsive ESI, who will review ESI for responsiveness/privilege, and methods of searching the ESI (e.g., keywords).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topics are appropriate for the mandatory discovery conference or when it becomes apparent ESI will be produced; addressing them early reduces disputes and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privilege/logging requirement when withholding documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A party withholding responsive documents on the basis of privilege must expressly make the claim and describe the nature of the documents, communications, or tangible things not produced or disclosed in a manner that, without revealing privileged information, will enable other parties to assess the claim (Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most common way to particularize privilege/protection is a privilege log identifying each withheld document, the nature of the privilege/protection claimed, names of communicants, date/place, and general subject matter. See advisory committee notes and case law for log content guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate method of responding to discovery disputes (meet-and-confer, not immediate motions)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is generally inappropriate to respond to discovery requests by filing motions attacking them (e.g., motions to strike or for protective order); the party ordinarily should respond and state reasons for objections and attempt to resolve disputes via meet-and-confer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board expects parties to indicate which requests they will permit and to state reasons for objections to those they believe improper; meet-and-confer obligations are required and failure may lead to sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to cooperate in discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party and its attorney/authorized representative has a duty to make a good faith effort to satisfy the discovery needs of its adversary and to seek only such discovery as is proper and relevant to the issues in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board looks with extreme disfavor on non-cooperation. Duty to cooperate is not excused by an adversary's failure to fulfill obligations; failure to cooperate can lead to warnings, burdening the Board with motions, or sanctions up to judgment. Parties should present positions with candor, specificity, and support during informal negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to conduct a discovery conference (cases commenced on/after Nov. 1, 2007)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are required to hold a conference to discuss settlement and plans for discovery, including the nature and basis of claims/defenses, possibility of settlement or modification of pleadings, and plans for disclosures and discovery (including Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f) subjects and any Board-required subjects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference must address discovery plans and trial evidence unless the case is settled. Parties must cooperate in scheduling; if a party refuses, contact the assigned Board attorney to facilitate scheduling. Topics may include ESI protocols and alternative resolution means such as Accelerated Case Resolution (ACR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and form of Requests for Admission (Fed. R. Civ. P. 36(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request admission of the truth of any matters within scope of Rule 26(b)(1) relating to (A) facts, application of law to fact, or opinions about either; and (B) genuineness of any described documents. Each matter must be separately stated, and a request to admit genuineness must be accompanied by a copy of the document unless previously furnished/made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for admission are useful to determine facts not in dispute and to facilitate introduction of documents produced in discovery. Scope is governed by Fed. R. Civ. P. 36(a) and Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to respond and effect of failing to respond to Requests for Admission
rubrics_metrics.description: A matter is admitted unless, within 30 days after being served, the party serves a written answer or objection (Fed. R. Civ. P. 36(a)(3)). Requests served during discovery must be responded to within 30 days; if no response, the requests stand admitted by operation of law unless excusable neglect is shown or a motion to withdraw/amend is filed and granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing/delivery rules (five extra days for mail/overnight) and no extra time for electronic service apply as with other discovery. A motion under Fed. R. Civ. P. 36(b) can seek withdrawal or amendment of admissions; courts consider excusable neglect under Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(b)(1)(B) for late response relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of answers to Requests for Admission
rubrics_metrics.description: If a matter is not admitted, the answer must specifically deny it or state in detail why the answering party cannot truthfully admit or deny it; denials must fairly respond to the substance. A party may assert lack of knowledge only if it states that it has made reasonable inquiry and that the information known or readily obtainable is insufficient to enable admission or denial (Fed. R. Civ. P. 36(a)(4)-(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If good faith requires qualification or partial denial, the answer must specify the part admitted and qualify or deny the rest. Grounds for objecting must be stated; a party may not object solely because the request presents a genuine issue for trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature of responses and counsel risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers and objections to requests for admission may be signed by the responding party or by its attorney. However, an attorney who signs answers or objections risks becoming a witness or disqualification from representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel should be aware that signing admissions/answers can create witness/disqualification issues under professional responsibility rules (see 37 CFR § 11.307 and relevant TTAB decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and scope of an admission
rubrics_metrics.description: Any matter admitted (expressly or by failure to timely respond) under Fed. R. Civ. P. 36(a) is conclusively established for the pending proceeding unless the Board permits withdrawal/amendment or reopening of time. An admission is only for the purpose of the pending proceeding and not for any other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A denial does not establish truth or falsity but leaves the matter for proof at trial. A motion under Fed. R. Civ. P. 36(b) and Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(b)(1)(B) provides mechanisms to relieve untimely responses; case law shows courts weigh prejudice and presentation of merits when deciding to grant withdrawal/amendment.
